content.value_statement: Video creators need reliable settings for short Wan 2.7 clips and lip-synced variants. This skill guides RunComfy CLI requests, prompt structure, limits, and model routing.
actual_capabilities: Runs Wan 2.7 text-to-video jobs through the RunComfy CLI.
Documents duration, resolution, aspect ratio, seed, and negative prompt fields.
Explains when to use an audio URL for lip-sync and when to omit it.
Shows prompt patterns for product, spokesperson, and vertical video clips.
Maps common RunComfy CLI exit codes to likely causes.
limitations: Requires RunComfy CLI, account access, and a valid token.
Outputs follow documented model limits, including 15 seconds and 1080p.
User prompts and media references are sent to RunComfy.
It does not generate voice tracks directly; audio must be supplied for lip-sync.

use_cases.title: Create Short Product Videos
use_cases.description: Marketing teams can turn product shot direction into 5 to 15 second clips with controlled aspect ratios.

use_cases.title: Produce Lip-Synced Spokesperson Clips
use_cases.description: Content teams can pair a voiceover URL with a close-up video prompt for social variants.

use_cases.title: Prototype Motion Concepts
use_cases.description: Design teams can compare seeds, prompt expansion, and negative prompts before final video production.

prompt_templates.title: Basic Wan 2.7 Clip
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a single short video.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a 5 second Wan 2.7 video prompt for this idea. Include camera motion, subject action, aspect ratio, and resolution.

prompt_templates.title: Vertical Social Variant
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft a vertical Wan 2.7 prompt for this campaign. Include one primary action, lighting direction, duration, and negative prompt guidance.

prompt_templates.title: Lip-Synced Spokesperson Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a Wan 2.7 lip-sync clip using my voiceover URL. Check audio requirements, recommend duration, and describe the camera setup.

prompt_templates.title: Model Routing And Safety Check
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced request before running a job.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this video request and decide whether Wan 2.7 is the right model. Flag privacy risks, shell quoting risks, and better model alternatives.

output_examples.input: Create a vertical cafe product video for a social post.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a focused 9:16 Wan 2.7 prompt with close-up camera motion, warm lighting, short duration, and concrete negative prompts.

output_examples.input: Make a spokesperson clip from my supplied voiceover.
output_examples.output: The skill checks audio length and format, suggests a locked close-up shot, and explains that the voiceover is sent to RunComfy.

output_examples.input: I need a brand-safe product showcase with exact wording.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends disabling prompt expansion, keeping one primary action, and using targeted negative prompts for unwanted visual artifacts.

best_practices: Keep each clip focused on one primary action.
Use concrete negative prompts for visible defects, not vague quality terms.
Confirm privacy expectations before sending prompts, voiceovers, or media URLs to RunComfy.
anti_patterns: Putting multiple unrelated actions into one short clip.
Using untrusted prompts directly inside a shell command string.
Expecting Wan 2.7 to create voice audio without a supplied track.

faq.question: What does this skill generate?
faq.answer: It helps generate short Wan 2.7 text-to-video clips through the RunComfy CLI.

faq.question: Does it support lip-sync?
faq.answer: Yes. It can use a supplied audio URL for lip-synced video when the file meets the documented limits.

faq.question: What tools are required?
faq.answer: You need the RunComfy CLI, a RunComfy account, and either a login session or a token.

faq.question: Can it make long videos?
faq.answer: No. The skill documents a 15 second model limit and suggests stitching clips for longer stories.

faq.question: Where does my prompt go?
faq.answer: The RunComfy CLI sends the prompt and media references to the RunComfy Model API.

faq.question: Can Claude, Codex, or Claude Code use it?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
